kicker: Hy-Nomas, an interactive video world model

scenes.headline: How a video model remembers the world it made
scenes.sub: Hy-Nomas: text and camera in, five seconds at a time.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Capstan! Hy-Nomas builds a video world you steer with words and a camera. Where does it keep its memory?

scenes.text: Generate five seconds at a time, and keep every past segment as attention keys and values, not as frames or 3D.
scenes.say: The idea: make five seconds at a time, and remember the past as attention keys and values. Not frames, not a map.

steps.say: A structured prompt goes through a Qwen text encoder.
Fifty-four transformer blocks denoise the new segment. Camera poses join one per latent frame.
Attention reaches back into the cache of every earlier segment, never forward.
The finished segment is decoded, and written into the cache.

items.say: Eight denoising steps, one forward each.
Mix a little noise back in, the way training saw its own history.
One more pass writes this segment's keys and values.

left.title: A true sliding window
left.say: A true sliding window would keep the newest eighteen frames: about three seconds.

right.title: What the 4090 preset does
items: Crowded near now, frame zero always
right.say: The single GPU preset picks eighteen from the whole past, crowded near now, always with the first. The rest waits in system memory.

steps.say: A revisit from the project's own demo. At eight seconds, a frozen waterfall.
The camera turns away and back. The waterfall returns; the ceiling around it does not.

scenes.label: of system memory per second of video, in the CPU archive
scenes.note: never trimmed; a minute is about 72 GB
scenes.say: That archive costs about one point two gigabytes of system memory per second of world, never trimmed.

scenes.title: How big is a lightweight LoRA?
scenes.say: The robotics adapter is three billion parameters, over a third of the model. Merged, it costs nothing extra.

scenes.text: The memory is the attention cache itself; one GPU holds a sample of it, and RAM holds the rest.
scenes.say: The memory is the attention cache. One GPU holds a sample; system memory holds the rest.

recap: The full archive grows in RAM
scenes.say: Five second segments, eighteen chosen frames, and a growing archive.
